intro.text: The king of Alethkar, son of the late King Gavilar Kholin.
The king of Alethkar and son of Gavilar Kholin, who leads the war of vengeance for his father on the Shattered Plains.
The king of Alethkar and son of Gavilar Kholin, killed in Kholinar while trying to save his wife and son.

items.text: Left in charge of the kingdom a year before Gavilar's death, Elhokar did a favour for his friend Roshone, a silversmith-owning lighteyes, by having two rival darkeyed silversmiths arrested on invented charges. He left them in prison, and they died there. They were Moash's grandparents.

After Gavilar was assassinated, Elhokar swore to avenge him on the Parshendi, who claimed the killing, and bound the highprinces to the Vengeance Pact. This held the kingdom together for a time. His messengers asking the Parshendi why they had done it got no answer.

In 1173 Elhokar led a greatshell hunt on the Shattered Plains. When a chasmfiend attacked, his saddle girth snapped and threw him, but he charged the beast anyway and was knocked down. Dalinar caught its claw and saved him, and the king held up the gemheart.
On the march back he urged Dalinar to use faster bridges like Sadeas's, and asked him to look into the cut saddle strap, insisting Dalinar doubted his fears.
In private Dalinar voiced his worry that the war was dragging on. Elhokar replied that the strategy was Dalinar's own and asked whether his uncle thought him a poor king.

At a feast Elhokar named Sadeas Highprince of Information and charged him with investigating the threats to his life. Sadeas reported that Dalinar was not involved, but that someone had planted weakened gemstones in the king's Shardplate.

Watching Adolin duel, Elhokar praised him above Gavilar and Dalinar. He accused Dalinar of still hinting at peace, wondered aloud who was truly behind Gavilar's murder, and said he saw villains' faces in mirrors.

After Sadeas's betrayal at the Tower, Dalinar confronted Elhokar in Plate. Overpowered, the king admitted he had cut his own saddle strap to draw attention to the danger he felt. Dalinar made him name him Highprince of War, and told him he was courting Navani.
Elhokar was impressed when Kaladin's bridgemen took over his guard. In council, he feared Dalinar's plans to have Adolin duel for Shards and to refound the Knights Radiant would break the kingdom.
After a highstorm a balcony railing gave way beneath him, and his guards caught him just in time. The railing had been cut with a Shardblade, and Elhokar insisted Kaladin take charge of his guards.
When Kaladin sensed danger in another storm, the king's party fled through the kitchens as the Assassin in White struck. Afterwards Elhokar praised Kaladin and assumed the assassin had come for him.
Elhokar and Dalinar questioned a madman brought from Kholinar who called himself Talenel'Elin, Herald of War, and carried a Shardblade.
Elhokar's council of highprinces dissolved into arguments over the assassin until Dalinar called for an expedition to end the war.

At Adolin's duel four opponents appeared instead of two, and Elhokar argued against pulling out. When Kaladin then insulted a highprince, the furious king wanted him executed, relenting only to have him jailed when Dalinar stood firm.

While Dalinar led the expedition, Elhokar stayed behind and visited Kaladin, asking how a man knows what to do and whether he was a bad king. Kaladin said yes, and Elhokar admitted the failure after the duel was his own.
That night Kaladin found Elhokar drunk, his guards replaced by plotters. A false guard stabbed the king in the side, and Kaladin fought Moash and Graves to protect him.
Elhokar hid with Lopen's family, whose mother fed him up, before the Herdazians brought him to the Oathgate and Urithiru.
Recovering from his wound, Elhokar blessed Dalinar and Navani's marriage for his mother's sake, remarking that Dalinar had always held the real power.
He told Dalinar he was a fine king but not an extraordinary one, and that Dalinar was better suited to rule. He planned to retake Kholinar and rescue his wife and son, with Kaladin to fly them there.
Elhokar confirmed Ialai's appointment of Amaram as regent of the Sadeas princedom, pressed Kaladin to promise the flight to Kholinar, and enjoyed a practice flight to the warcamps.
Shallan offered him her team of spies and illusions, and he formally asked Dalinar for her to join the mission.
Kaladin flew the team to besieged Kholinar. Disguised by Shallan as a lighteyed woman, Elhokar told Kaladin he expected to fail and ordered him to save the city if he did.
From the tailor Yokska he learned of riots and of Queen Aesudan withdrawing from view. Elhokar struggled to accept it and was resolved to rescue her, drawing maps and assigning tasks to the team.
Wearing an illusion of General Khal, he courted the city's lighteyes. He told Shallan he could still be a hero for the city and his son, and she drew him looking truly regal.
On the eve of the assault Elhokar revealed himself and won a hundred soldiers. As drums sounded, he ordered the march on the palace and quietly sent a spanreed to alert Urithiru.
Elhokar led the palace assault with Adolin and Azure, then climbed with Kaladin to find Aesudan, who was not herself. Hearing his son scream, he rushed to take the boy.
Before he could finish speaking, Moash ran him through with a spear and killed him.
Hoid found a Cryptic hiding near where he fell. Elhokar's body was burned with honours.

appearance.text: A handsome, clean-shaven Alethi with tan skin and green eyes, full lips, a broad forehead and a firm chin. He resembles his father, though with fewer scars.

personality.text: He loves maps, keeps a large gallery of them and draws his own when needed.
Fearful of assassins since his father's murder, he wears his Shardplate far more than other Shardbearers and chafes at comparisons with Gavilar.
Not a great leader, he nonetheless has buried potential: he can act decisively, has a feel for politics, and slowly learns to face his own flaws.
